DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph JUL 26 ERNESTO BRILLANTES Vista Verde Executive Village Cainta, Rizal Dear Mr. Brillantes: . 2024 30 JUL This has reference to your letter dated 29 May legal opinion on whether the ordinance of the Municipal Ordinance of Cainta, Rizal restricting the construction of apartment dwelling in your privately-owned residential lot is valid. According to your representation, you contacted the Engineering Department of the Cainta Local Government to confirm that the aforementioned ordinance exists. You indicated that the Engineering Department responded that such an ordinance exists and is currently in effect to regulate the influx of residents. Thus, the request for legal opinion and the request to call the attention of the Municipal Mayor regarding the matter. At the onset, please be informed that this department is precluded from acting on queries which are presumptively valid acts. DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated 17 September 2010 specifically provides: "xxx all concerned are hereby advised that the Department shall not an act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: Xxx 2. Those presumptively valid acts, e.g. enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already eniov the presumption of reqularitv on the part of the public officer concerned and similar instances• Xxxx" (Emphasis and underlining supplied) Moreover, it is to be emphasized that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare any ordinance or resolution approved by local government officials invalid, nor does it have authority to declare invalid or illegal acts committed by local government officials which is alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code or any other applicable laws. The same must be threshed out before the proper forum. Moreover, the Department does not act on queries which involves presumptively valid acts; e.g. enacted ordinance consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances. However, for the purpose of academic discussion coupled with our objective to guide the concerned on the proper course of action to take under circumstances, we deem it necessary to indulge in disquisition on the laws applicable to the matter, Thus, we invite your attention to the case of Social Justice Society V. Hon. Jose L. Atienza Jr. 1 where the Supreme Court ruled: ' G.R. No. 156052. February 13, 2008 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No: 8876-34-54

"Statutes and ordinances are presumed valid unless and until the courts declare the contrary in clear and unequivocal terms. The mere fact that the ordinance is alleged to be unconstitutional or invalid will not entitle a party to have its enforcement enjoined. The presumption is all in favor of validity. The reason for this is obvious: The action of the elected representatives of the people cannot be lightly set aside. The councilors must. in the very nature of thinqs. be familiar with the necessities of their particular municipality and with all the facts and circumstances which surround the subject and necessitate action. The local legislative body, by enacting the ordinance, has in effect given notice that the regulations are essential to the well-being of the people . The Judiciary should not lightly set aside legislative action when there is not a clear invasion of personal or property rights under the guise of police regulation." (Emphasis supplied) From the foregoing, municipal ordinances are accorded the presumption of validity, unless declared invalid by the proper tribunal, because the legislature is presumed to abide by the Constitution.2 Likewise, it cannot be denied that Local Government Units have the authority, derived from the police power, of restricting the construction of any building to safeguard inhabitants as the LGUs see proper. Further, any issues concerning the legality or validity of a law shall be threshed out by filing a special civil action for declaratory relief before the proper court in accordance with Section I, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court, which provides and we quote: Section 1. Who may file petition. — Any person interested under a deed, will, contract or other written instrument, or whose rights are affected by a statute, executive order or regulation, ordinance, or any other governmental regulation may, before breach or violation thereof bring an action in the appropriate Regional Trial Court to determine any question of construction or validity arising, and for a declaration of his rights or duties, thereunder. Finally, we respectfully reiterate that this Department is bereft of authority to rule on the legality and validity of Ordinance of the Municipality of Cainta. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you Very truly yours, BY AU ORITY OF THE S ETARY: AN VICTOR R. LLAMAS U e ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/JVRWLLLS-LRALLD/lasm Ibid Page 2 of 2
